newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends softer after rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends softer after rate cut.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed slightly lower against the dollar on Thursday and banks remained cautious after the two percentage-point cut in the Central Bank's overnight rates.
Banks believe speculation has not yet died down and a further lowering of the Central Bank's overnight rate may rekindle this, traders said.
The peso ended at 26.375 from 26.374, with volume higher at $202 million from $180.7 million.
"The situation is still wobbly. There is still negative sentiment in Asia," a foreign bank dealer said.
The peso was a victim of the recent Asian currency turmoil which was caused by the problems of the Thai baht. This forced the Central Bank to raise its overnight borrowing last week.
In late deals, the Central Bank had to unload $27 million at 26.375, traders said.
Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson earlier told Reuters the Central Bank would bring down overnight rates to normal levels next week if market conditions stabilise.
